discovery: Evidence for a nanohertz gravitational-wave background using pulsar timing arrays

nominees.name: Michael Kramer
nominees.affiliation: Max Planck Institute for Radio Astronomy, Bonn, Germany (EPTA)

motivation: Decades of precision timing of millisecond pulsars have turned the Galaxy into a gravitational-wave detector. In 2023 the NANOGrav, EPTA/InPTA, PPTA and CPTA collaborations independently reported a common red-noise process showing the Hellings-Downs angular correlation, the signature of a nanohertz gravitational-wave background. This opens an entirely new frequency band, complementary to LIGO and the future LISA. Whether the signal comes from supermassive black-hole binaries or from early-universe physics such as first-order phase transitions or cosmic strings, it already constrains fundamental theory quantitatively. McLaughlin, Kramer and Manchester built and led the timing programmes, instrumentation and analysis methods that made this long, patient measurement possible. This is a community effort sustained over twenty years, and these three represent its scientific leadership.
